units.text: Rain drums on the corrugated roof.
Somewhere a forklift beeps, backing up, backing up, never arriving.
Sodium light buzzes over the sorting belt.
He stands at the belt with a scanner, eighteen, new vest still creased.
She watches him from the mezzanine stairs and does not come down.
Seven weeks. That's what the last kid lasted. Seven weeks, and he cried in the van park like it was a funeral. You want to know what I told him?
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: I told him the belt doesn't care. That's the whole job. It doesn't care that your mother's sick, or that you wanted to be a drummer, or that you're clever. It just keeps coming, and the only thing you get to decide is whether you flinch.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Water finds a gap in the roof and ticks into a bucket.
Nobody has emptied the bucket in a long time.
He lifts a parcel, scans it, sets it down.
Marguerite. Nobody uses it. Scan the next one.
units.name: THE WOMAN
